small_guidance:
- The conv_transpose dominates runtime (the GAP+BN epilogue is already fused and tiny). Tuning BLOCK_S/num_warps further on `_gap_affine_kernel` will not move the needle — focus elsewhere.
- If keeping the current structure, drop the explicit `x.contiguous().view(N,C,S)` (which forces a layout copy back from channels_last_3d after the conv) — instead launch the kernel directly on the channels_last tensor by passing strides, so the post-conv copy is eliminated.
- Add a small autotune over `BLOCK_S` ∈ {2048, 4096, 8192} with num_warps {4,8} keyed on S only; current S=20*36*36=25920 so BLOCK_S=4096 with num_warps=8 is likely optimal.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose3d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: one program per `(N, IC tile, input-spatial tile)` computing the outer product `input[n,ic,d,h,w] * weight[ic,oc,kd,kh,kw]` and atomically scattering into the output grid at `(d+kd, h+kh, w+kw)` with the appropriate stride/padding offsets. This is the high-headroom move since cuDNN's ConvTranspose3d is the bottleneck.
- Better: fuse the scale + BN-affine + global-average-pool into the conv-transpose epilogue so the full DHW output volume is never materialized. Each program accumulates its partial contribution to a per-(N,OC) sum in shared memory / atomics, then a tiny second kernel divides by S and applies `A*mean+B`. This collapses the 16×128×20×36×36 ≈ 53M-element intermediate entirely.
- Alternatively, since GAP commutes with the affine and with the conv-transpose's linear structure, you can compute `sum_over_output(convT(x))[n,oc] = sum_{ic,d,h,w} x[n,ic,d,h,w] * sum_{kd,kh,kw} W[ic,oc,kd,kh,kw]` only on the *interior* output region where every kernel tap lands in-bounds; the border region needs per-position handling. But this is an algebraic shortcut and violates the safety contract — do NOT do this. Stick with materialized scatter-add then reduce.
